subject: Culture
title: Chinese New Year
description: Learn Chinese New Year in one minute.

hook.text: Every Chinese New Year triggers the largest human migration on Earth. Three billion trips in one season.

buildup.text: The festival follows the lunar calendar and lasts 15 days, ending with the Lantern Festival.

discovery.text: Red envelopes, firecrackers, and lion dances all trace back to a myth about chasing away a monster called Nian.

twist.text: China tried replacing it with Gregorian New Year after 1949. People ignored the change and kept celebrating.

climax.text: No government decree could override a tradition rooted in family, food, and the lunar cycle.

punchline.text: The moon outranks the calendar every year.

quiz.question: According to legend, what creature do firecrackers and red decorations ward off?

details.summary: Chinese New Year, the world's largest annual human migration, sends hundreds of millions of people home to their families. This 15-day festival marks the lunar new year with firecrackers to ward off evil, red envelopes of money, family reunions, and traditions stretching back over 3,000 years.
details.whyItMatters: Chinese New Year shapes global economics — factories close, supply chains pause, and billions of dollars move through red envelopes. It is the cultural heartbeat of 1.4 billion people.
takeaways: Chinese New Year causes the world's largest annual human migration
Red envelopes contain money gifts based on lucky number amounts
The festival lasts 15 days, ending with the Lantern Festival

faq.question: Why are firecrackers essential to Chinese New Year?
faq.answer: Legend says the monster Nian attacked villages every new year. Villagers discovered it feared loud noises and the color red. Firecrackers combine both — loud explosions and red paper casings — to drive away evil spirits and bad luck.

faq.question: How do red envelopes work?
faq.answer: Red envelopes (hongbao) containing money are given by married couples to unmarried younger relatives. Amounts must be even numbers (odd numbers are for funerals) and avoid the number four (sounds like death). Eight is particularly lucky.
